name: Mayoruna-Jandiatuba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; only early wordlists (de Alviano 1957; Martius 1867) — nothing plausibly covering stress

sources.citation: González, Carolina. 2016 [2017]. Tipología de los sistemas métricos de veinticinco lenguas pano. Amerindia 39: 129-172.
sources.note: Panoan stress typology; Tabla 1 lists Matsés (final, non-cohesive), Matis (final iambic), Kulina, Korubo etc. for the Mayoruna branch but has no entry for the extinct Mayoruna of the Jandiatuba; Alviano not cited.

sources.citation: Martius, C.F.P. von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens II: Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium. Leipzig. pp. 236-239 (Maxuruna / Mayoruna lists) — named in the earlier scan note.
sources.note: Not this language: Martius reproduces Castelnau's Amazon-River Mayoruna lists and Spix's Tabatinga 'Maxuruna' (Glottolog mayo1271 / Mayoruna of Tabatinga), not the Jandiatuba variety, which is attested only by Alviano 1957. No accent remarks anyway.

sources.citation: Oliveira, Sanderson Castro Soares de. 2014. Contribuições para a reconstrução do Protopáno. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília.
sources.note: Mentions '†Mayoruna of the Jandiatuba River' only inside Fleck's reproduced classification; no data or stress statement for it.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH.
sources.note: Nothing for this language. Table of sources: '†Mayoruna of the Jandiatuba River – Alviano (1957: 44–56) 503-word lexicon; complete reproduction: Fleck (in prep.) reproduction and phonology' (unpublished). Location note: Jandiatuba R., migrated from Ucayali via Javari (Alviano 1957: 43).

sources.citation: Alviano, Frei Fidelis de. 1957 [impr. 1958]. Ensaios da língua dos índios Magironas ou Maiorunas do rio Jandiatuba (Alto Solimões). Revista do Instituto Histórico e Geográfico Brasileiro 237 (out.-dez. 1957): 43-60. Rio de Janeiro: Departamento de Imprensa Nacional.
sources.note: Nothing. The only phonetic remarks (p. 43, 'LINGUA DOS MAGIRONAS') are: 'Todos os sons da língua dos Magironas poderão ser representados pela fonética portuguêsa, como foi dito (falando do idioma dos Ticunas)' plus a note that S and C are dental as in Castilian and are written Z, Ç. Then a ~500-item Portuguese-Mayoruna wordlist (pp. 44-56) and ethnographic notes (pp. 56-60). The Mayoruna forms carry Portuguese-style accent marks, which by the author's own convention (stated in his 1944 Ticuna grammar, to which p. 43 refers) mark the tonic vowel; a script census of the scanned list gives the w…

sources.citation: Alviano, Frei Fidelis de. 1944 [impr. 1945]. Gramática, dicionário, verbos e frases e vocabulário prático da língua dos índios Ticunas. Revista do Instituto Histórico e Geográfico Brasileiro 183 (abr.-jun. 1944): 3 ff. (Primeira seção 'Regras de pronúncia', 'Notações ortográficas', printed pp. 13-16).
sources.note: About TICUNA and about Alviano's notation only (the convention the 1957 Mayoruna article points back to): p. 15 'Podemos contudo dizer e estabelecer como regra que, como na língua portuguêsa, na língua dos Ticunas uma palavra é paroxítona quando não leva acento... Para maior clareza, marcaremos, todavia, com acento a vogal tônica de cada palavra'. Establishes that his acute accents mark the stressed vowel; says nothing about Mayoruna.

sources.citation: Oliveira, Sanderson Castro Soares de. 2023. Las primeras escisiones de la familia Pano: una propuesta de subagrupamiento en una familia de la Amazonia occidental. IJAL 89(3): 289-331.

sources.note: Most recent comparative treatment of the Mayoruna branch listed by Glottolog for this languoid; may phonologize Alviano's forms (and comment on his accent marks) when using them as cognate evidence. Unlikely but not excluded to contain a stress remark.

sources.citation: Fleck, David W. In preparation (cited in Fleck 2013: 11, AMNH Anthropological Papers 99). Complete reproduction and phonological interpretation of Alviano's (1957) Mayoruna of the Jandiatuba River lexicon (part of his comparative Mayoruna phonology).
